source.title: AdaFamily: A family of Adam-like adaptive gradient methods

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers and reports test errors on natural image-classification datasets, bearing on V4; it uses a different experimental comparison from the version's benchmark evidence.
record.gate_note: The study reports test errors for optimizer variants on three datasets and four architectures. It does not report training error, random-label fitting, or a train–test gap. It tests V4 only through the adaptive-optimizer held-out-performance comparison.
record.test_reason: The experiments compare adaptive optimizers with other adaptive optimizers to evaluate AdaFamily. They contain no SGD or momentum-SGD baseline, so they cannot establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD difference or whether decoupled weight decay recovers it. No other version is tested. The missing comparison is untested scope, not evidence limiting V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: AdaFamily variants outperform the compared adaptive optimizers in most cases, with smaller µ generally preferred for ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 and larger µ for MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet-B0. This is a statement about selected variants, not every AdaFamily variant.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a newly proposed Adam-like optimizer family against Adam and related adaptive methods on image-classification datasets; the experiments do not use the original version's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The best-performing µ varies by network family: smaller µ values perform better for ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121; larger µ values perform better for MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet-B0. Test errors also differ across dataset and architecture conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive-optimizer test errors vary with architecture, dataset and AdaFamily's µ. An AdaFamily variant is best or second best in every tested architecture–dataset combination, but no SGD comparison is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the paper's fixed training recipe, selected AdaFamily variants compete with or outperform the tested adaptive optimizers on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN.

record.problems: No training errors or train–test gaps are reported. The experiments do not compare with SGD or momentum SGD, and report averaged results over 10 runs without error bars or other uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization; chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.

Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited tuning; comparisons of training performance; broader tuning; recovery relative to SGD through decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers; language benchmarks.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows omit a relevant recipe detail: every optimizer except Adam uses decoupled weight decay. Learning rates and other hyperparameters are fixed at stated defaults rather than tuned. Results average ten runs without uncertainty estimates. Training errors are unreported, but their absence alone would not prevent testing V4 if a suitable SGD comparison existed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization alongside it, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.

No SGD or momentum-SGD comparison; no language benchmarks, equal-training-performance analysis, broad tuning comparison, Adam-to-SGD switch, or evaluation of whether broader tuning removes the difference.
Large versus small batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Sharpness or other generalization measures and their relationship to train–test gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The four tested architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN, under the stated training recipe
reader_labels.reason: Test errors vary by architecture and dataset, and no SGD comparison is given; these results do not establish the version's claimed adaptive-versus-SGD generalization difference (R1–R12).
